headline: CBA's cash NPAT increased $313 million or 6% to $5,445 million in 1H26 versus 1H25 ($5,132 million), driven by strong operating income growth of $924 million (7%), partially offset by higher underlying operating expenses of $348 million (5%), notable/restructuring items of $170 million (vs nil in 1H25), and higher tax expense of $94 million (4%). Loan impairment expense was broadly flat, decreasing by just $1 million. Statutory NPAT increased $270 million or 5% to $5,412 million, $43 million below the cash movement due to non-cash items moving from a $10 million tailwind in 1H25 to a $33 million headwind in 1H26 (primarily hedging/IFRS volatility and disposal transaction costs).

drivers.narrative: NII increased $761 million or 6% to $12,695 million, primarily driven by a $96 billion or 8% increase in average interest earning assets to $1,232 billion (home loans +$31 billion, business and corporate loans +$29 billion), partly offset by a 4 basis point decrease in NIM to 2.04%. The margin decline was driven by asset pricing (down 2 bpts from home and business lending competition), funding costs (down 3 bpts from declining rates and deposit competition), partially offset by capital/replicating portfolio (up 6 bpts) and portfolio mix (up 1 bpt).

Other operating income increased $163 million or 8% to $2,326 million. Key drivers: commissions up $61 million (6%) to $1,146 million from higher insurance income including a CommInsure milestone payment and equities volumes; lending fees up $16 million (4%) to $465 million from syndication and institutional lending; trading income up $84 million (16%) to $603 million from Markets gains and favourable derivative valuation adjustments; funds management up $7 million (12%) to $67 million; partly offset by other income down $5 million (10%) from lower Structured Asset Finance revenue following aircraft lease portfolio sale.

Underlying operating expenses increased $348 million or 5% to $6,720 million. Staff expenses rose $169 million (4%) to $4,139 million from wage inflation and increased FTE (49,307 to 51,755, +2,448) for technology, retail lenders, and fraud prevention. IT services expenses increased $134 million (11%) to $1,321 million from cloud computing volumes, software licensing, and AI infrastructure investment. Occupancy up $5 million (1%) to $465 million. Other expenses up $40 million (5%) to $795 million from higher marketing spend.

Notable/restructuring items were $170 million in 1H26 versus nil in 1H25. These relate to provisions for the settlement of legal proceedings in New Zealand, an additional goodwill payment made to certain customers as a result of ASIC's Better Banking review, and domestic customer remediation.

Loan impairment expense decreased $1 million to $319 million (from $320 million in 1H25), essentially flat. The decrease was driven by improvements in business credit quality and easing conditions for households, partly offset by elevated geopolitical tensions and global macroeconomic uncertainty. Home loan 90+ day arrears decreased 7 bpts to 0.63%, supported by interest rate reductions and tax refunds.

Corporate tax expense increased $94 million or 4% to $2,367 million, reflecting a 30.3% effective tax rate (down from 30.7% in 1H25). The ETR decrease was primarily due to a decrease in non-deductible expenses in 1H26, partially offset by higher profit before tax driving the absolute tax increase.

limitations: No walk/bridge chart of cash NPAT movement was found in either document; component movements are computed from period columns in results tables rather than read from a bank-published decomposition.

The statutory-to-cash reconciliation shows non-cash items of -$33m in 1H26 (vs +$10m in 1H25), explaining the $43m gap between cash ($313m) and statutory ($270m) NPAT growth, but these are not year-on-year drivers.
Notable items in 1H25 were zero, making the delta straightforward; however, the composition differs materially from 2H25 which included Bankwest restructuring.
Expenses are claimed on the underlying/notable split; the bank equally publishes the combined headline framing, so both claims are capped at 80.
